title: Choose FINN's visual world
question: The roll assigned Bombay Deco. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. (Code-led: each card shows a phone sketch of the Brief.)

options.label: Bombay Deco
options.lineage: 1930s Art Deco of Marine Drive and the Fort, Mumbai's money district
options.thesis: The street FINN's investor works on, built in setbacks: what matters most stands tallest.
options.viewport: Sea-green app bar with FINN in condensed deco caps; a pale stone ground; the day's count; the one most material story on a reversed sea-green plate with a stepped crown; ranked rows each carrying a 1-3 step setback mark; Material nav bar Brief / Watch / Ask.
options.risk: Deco slides into heritage costume (sunbursts, gold, cinema signage) unless the setback stays one functional mark.

raised.raise: Rank by weight, case and one reversed plate per screen, not by piling on sizes: only the single most material story gets the sea-green plate.
Every story keeps its exchange reference (NSE sequence and filed time) as its catalogue number, so the citation is always one glance away.
Each holding carries fixed furniture (weight, last close, setback rank) in the same place on every screen.
One display face at exactly three steps (screen title, ticker, lead headline); everything else is the UI face.
No deco ornament beyond the setback: type and colour carry the world.

options.label: Exchange Intimation
options.lineage: BSE/NSE Regulation 30 intimation letters and exchange acknowledgement stamps
options.thesis: FINN answers in the exchange's own paperwork: every finding stamped as received, with its reference.
options.viewport: White ground under a letterhead rule with the FINN wordmark; each story set as an intimation entry (Ref, scrip, filed time); material ones carry a violet 'received 10:57 IST' stamp; Material nav bar.
options.risk: The most literal reading of the subject; it can read bureaucratic, and it's where most filing-grounded runs land.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.lineage: scholarly reference editions drawn by a ruling engine
options.thesis: Every claim hangs on its source: citations run down a vermilion rail beside the text they ground.
options.viewport: Bone ground, small dense roman; on the Brief each story's citation keys run in a vermilion outboard rail; detents mark rank; Material nav bar.
options.case: Fuses well on the brain and dossier, where citations belong in a margin; loses audience identification, and a phone can't hold twin columns.
options.risk: Scholarly rather than Dalal Street; at 390px the rail must go outboard and the form loses its centre.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight, case and reversal.
options.viewport: Raked slides of stories along one axis.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the rake fights a phone list and investors don't read timetables.
options.kept: Rank by weight, case and one reversed plate per screen.
options.risk: Novelty geometry on a working screen.

options.label: Factory Catalogue
options.thesis: Everything is a numbered catalogue entry.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coding names as colour hides the companies the investor is looking for.
options.kept: Every story keeps its exchange reference as its catalogue number.
options.risk: Withholds names on purpose; wrong for triage.

options.label: Character Goods Catalogue
options.thesis: A finite ranked roster with fixed personal furniture.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful register breaks the professional standard.
options.kept: Each holding has fixed furniture in the same place everywhere.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: One face repeated at strict size steps.
options.case: Fuses poorly: pixel display type costs legibility for no product gain.
options.kept: One display face at exactly three steps.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.viewport: Giant glyph over a breathing grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type demo, not an investor's tool.
options.kept: No ornament beyond the one signature mark.

canonCard.label: The Indian broker-app standard
canonCard.thesis: What Kite, Groww and INDmoney ship: Material 3, white, navy and blue, green and red.
canonCard.viewport: Top app bar, portfolio summary card, then a list of filing cards with coloured chips; bottom nav bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every broker app by design.
